name: Vitamin B1 (Thiamine)
summary: A water-soluble coenzyme (thiamine pyrophosphate) central to carbohydrate metabolism and ATP production; nervous and cardiac tissue depend on it heavily.

conditions.label: Deficiency (beriberi / Wernicke-Korsakoff)
conditions.description: Impaired oxidative metabolism harms high-energy tissues: peripheral nerves, heart and brain.

affects.detail: Length-dependent sensorimotor neuropathy causes tingling, burning feet, weakness and loss of reflexes.
Peripheral vasodilation and myocardial dysfunction cause oedema, breathlessness and high-output cardiac failure.
Acute triad of confusion, ophthalmoplegia and ataxia; untreated it progresses to the irreversible amnesia of Korsakoff syndrome.

ageModifiers.adult: Classically precipitated by chronic alcohol use or malnutrition; give thiamine before glucose to avoid precipitating Wernicke encephalopathy.
ageModifiers.infant: Infantile beriberi can occur in breastfed infants of thiamine-deficient mothers, with acute cardiac and neurological collapse.
